sentences.text:
on 25 January,
2016  -1-  M. Cr. C. No.1542/2009 25/01/2016  Shri Ankit Premchandani, learned counsel for the petitioners.
Shri Milind Phadke, learned counsel for the respondent/State.

The petitioners before this Court have filed present petition under Sec.482 of Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment of complaint pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class, Indore filed by the respondent No.1 for offences under Sec.7(i), 14(a) read with Sec.16(1)(a)(i) and 16(1)(c) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

The petitioners' contention is that as per the case of prosecution Shri Sachin Logaria, Food Inspector visited the shop of the petitioners on 29/11/2007 and took samples of 'Jaora Gold Rawa'
and 'Best Choice Besan'.
In respect of Porridge (Rawa), the date of packing was October, 2007 and for Gram Flour (Besan) the date of packing was November 2007.
The best before date provided on the pouch in case of Porridge was 60 days from the date of packing and in case of Gram Flour it was 3 months from the date of packing.

A memo was drawn in Form No.IV under Rule 12 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules,
1955.
The petitioners have further stated that Porridge and Gram Flour was sent for analysis and a report from Laboratory was obtained on 14/12/2007.
The petitioners have further stated that for the first time vide letter dated 29/12/2008 which was actually received by the petitioners on 15/01/2009.
The report was forwarded to the petitioner on 15/01/2009 and the petitioner for the first time came to know about the report and the prosecution on 15/01/2009.

The petitioners have further stated that the products were also packed in pouches and each pouch was printed with the date of manufacture of product in question, the best before date and the name of manufacturer was also very much in existence.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has argued that once the shelf life of the sample seized was over,
the question of making a request by the petitioner for reanalysis does not arise and in light of the judgment delivered by this Court in the case of Prahlad Gattani and Others Vs. State of M.P.
reported in 2012(4) MPLJ 617.

entities.text:
Prahlad Gattani and Others Vs. State of M.P.
reported in 2012(4) MPLJ 617
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the entire complaint itself deserves to be quashed.

This Court has carefully gone through the aforesaid judgment and has heard learned counsel Government Advocate at length and in light of the aforesaid judgment, this Court is of the opinion that as the notice was issued only after expiry of shelf life, the complaint itself deserves to be quahsed.

sentences.text: Lastly reliance has been placed upon a judgment delivered in the case of Venkateshwaran Narayanan Ayyar and Others Vs. State of M.P. reported in 2006(2) MPLJ 592 and it has been argued that the petitioners were not responsible for the conduct of the business of the Company who has manufactured Porridge and Gram Flour and therefore, no case is made out against them.

entities.text: Venkateshwaran Narayanan Ayyar and Others Vs. State of M.P. reported in 2006(2) MPLJ 592
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the considered opinion of this Court and keeping in view the judgment delivered in the case of Prahlad Gattani (Supra) as the report of public analysis was forwarded after expiry of shelf life i.e.
on 15/01/2009, the question of permitting the respondent No.1 to proceed ahead with the complaint does not arise.

The right conferred upon the accused persons to make an application to the Court for sending the second part of the sample to the laboratory is no longer available to the accused persons as the shelf life is already over.
Resultantly, Criminal Case No.33965/2008 and other proceedings based upon the complaint are hereby quashed and the petitioner preferred under Sec.482 Cr.P.C. is allowed.
C. C. as per rules.
